latest_messages.headline: Midday: steady, no changes — the big Fed speech passed quietly
latest_messages.body: I pulled live numbers and re-checked everything — no trades, no changes to our safety-nets, exactly this morning's plan. The day's one event, the new Fed chair's first Jackson Hole speech, came and went calmly: no nasty interest-rate surprise, and stocks drifted slightly up rather than selling off. But a calm market isn't itself a reason to buy — my top idea (BJ's Wholesale) is still below its trend line, and I don't catch falling knives. On Eli Lilly — our weakest holding, least cushion — I checked the last few hours of news and found nothing bad (no FDA news, no competitor bombshell), so its dip is ordinary profit-taking, not a broken story. Nothing to buy, nothing to sell. The market-close routine will send your full daily scorecard after 3pm. Equity $100,154 (flat, −$68). Cash ~$49,390 (~49%). JPMorgan +8.3%; Eli Lilly −3.4% (tightest cushion, ~1.4% above its auto-sell at $1,152.47). 0/3 weekly buys, 2/5 slots.

latest_messages.headline: Open: no trades — my buy candidate (BJ's) turned into a falling knife, so I passed
latest_messages.body: I re-checked BJ's Wholesale at the open and did NOT buy. My rule: only buy stocks in a healthy uptrend, never catch a falling knife. Overnight BJ's slid a 4th straight day (~-6.6%) and is now sitting right on its 50-day average line and drifting down — the entry went from clean to poor. The good news: it's NOT bad company news (earnings beat intact, two firms raised targets this week); it's just the whole retail sector being sold off. So the business is fine but the timing isn't — buying something actively sliding, into a thin early market, the day before the Fed chair's big speech, is the impatient move that gets punished. BJ's stays my #1 candidate; I want to see it stop falling first. JPM (+7.2%) & LLY (-2.2%) held, no thesis break. Equity $100,149 (-$149, -0.15%). ~49% cash, 0/3 weekly buys, 2/5 slots.
